statements.note: The freeway comes from the heading "Driving along a freeway"; the purpose "leaving the other lanes clear for passing" is written as a reason.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN (it is night OR the driver is driving in [?poor conditions]) AND the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing the other vehicle

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.

flags.note: The heading does not say which conditions count as poor.

statements.note: Night and poor conditions come from the heading "Turn on headlights at night and in poor conditions". This fits the night passing steps (m40a), where high beams go on once alongside.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

statements.text: a cyclist MAY use any part of the lane to discourage passing WHEN the lane is [?too narrow to be shared safely] ONLY IF it is [?necessary for safety]

sources.quote: Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely
However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:

flags.span: too narrow to be shared safely
flags.note: No lane width is given.
The passage leaves it to the cyclist to judge when this is necessary.

flags.span: However, they can use any part of the lane
flags.note: "However" implies an unstated default position for cyclists in the lane that this permission departs from.

statements.note: "They" is read as cyclists from the heading "Cyclists". The list lead (m54) gives the permission and its condition to this item.

statements.text: a driver of a motor vehicle MUST keep a distance of at least 1 m between the vehicle and the cyclist, [?where practical], WHILE passing a cyclist IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.
(See Diagram 2-11.) Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.
bike lane adjacent to parking bays

flags.note: The passage does not say when keeping 1 m is not practical.

statements.note: The penalty comes from m57. Diagram 2-11's alt text reads "bike lane adjacent to parking bays", but the attached image shows a car passing a cyclist with 1 m marked between them.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN it is [?possible]

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: The passage does not say when changing lanes is not possible.

flags.span: you should change lanes to pass
flags.note: m51 gives the same advice for motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds without the hedge.

statements.note: The cyclist comes from the heading "Cyclists" and the sentences before (m56).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn [?unnecessarily] WHEN passing a cyclist BECAUSE the horn may frighten the cyclist and cause the cyclist to lose control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: The passage does not say when the horn is necessary.
Uses "overtaking" where most passages say "passing".

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly WHEN about to pass a cyclist AND the driver [?feels that the driver must use the horn] WHILE the driver is still [?some distance] away from the cyclist

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.span: feels that the driver must use the horn
flags.note: The need for the horn is left to the driver's feeling.

statements.force_from: imperative ("do not cut in front closely")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in [?closely] in front of a large vehicle WHEN passing the large vehicle BECAUSE cutting in is discourteous and dangerous AND cutting in reduces the space cushion that large vehicles require to stop [?safely]

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: No distance is given.
The passage does not say how much space a safe stop needs.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow [?more room] WHEN passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: The passage does not say how much more room, or more than what.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence BECAUSE of various factors such as air pressure and airflow

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.text: FACT the air turbulence created by a large vehicle may affect a driver's ability to control the vehicle WHEN the driver is passing the large vehicle

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.note: "May affect" is a possibility, so this is a FACT.

statements.force_from: imperative ("Stay well back and do not pass until")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay [?well back] from farm machinery AND SHOULD NOT pass the farm machinery UNTIL it is [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: No following distance is given.
The passage does not say what makes passing farm machinery safe.

statements.note: Farm machinery comes from the heading "Farm machinery".

statements.force_from: imperative ("only pass when it is safe to do so")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass a horse-drawn vehicle ONLY IF it is [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

flags.note: The passage does not say what makes passing a horse-drawn vehicle safe.

statements.note: The horse-drawn vehicle comes from the heading "Horse-drawn vehicles". The first half of the sentence is about following distance, not passing, and is not written.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD leave [?as much distance as possible] between the vehicle and the horse-drawn vehicle WHILE passing a horse-drawn vehicle BECAUSE passing [?too closely] could scare or startle the horse, causing the horse to change direction suddenly on the roadway

sources.quote: When passing, give as much distance between you and them as possible. Passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway.

flags.note: No distance is given.
The passage does not say how close is too close.

statements.note: "Them" is read as the horse-drawn vehicle of the heading "Horse-drawn vehicles".

statements.text: FACT in Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus

sources.quote: In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

statements.note: "Can report" is read as describing enforcement, not as a permission to drivers. The illegality comes from the duty to stop for a school bus (c1a).

statements.text: FACT pavement markings tell drivers when it is not [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Pavement markings divide traffic lanes, show turning lanes, mark pedestrian crossings, indicate obstacles and tell you when it is not safe to pass.

flags.note: The passage does not say what makes passing unsafe; m21 and m23 give the markings.

statements.note: Only the passing function of pavement markings is in this topic.

statements.text: FACT a solid line at the left of a driver's lane means it is [?unsafe] to pass

sources.quote: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass. ('A' should not pass.)
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

flags.note: The marking states a judgment of safety without saying why or for how far.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN there is a solid line at the left of the driver's lane

sources.quote: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass. ('A' should not pass.)
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

statements.note: From the example "('A' should not pass.)"; Diagram 3-2 shows car A with solid yellow lines at the left of its lane.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass WHEN there is a broken line at the left of the driver's lane ONLY IF the way is clear AND there are [?enough] broken lines ahead to complete the pass [?safely]

sources.quote: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear. ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)
vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

flags.note: No length of broken line is given.
The passage does not say what makes completing the pass safe.

statements.note: The second condition comes from the example about car A in the same passage; Diagram 3-3 shows car A behind a truck with broken yellow lines at the left of its lane.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass WHEN the driver is on a road where a "do not pass" sign is posted

statements.text: a driver MUST keep to the right-hand lane WHEN the driver is on a two-lane section where climbing or passing lanes are provided AND a "keep to the right lane except when passing" sign applies UNLESS the driver is passing

statements.note: The caption is a plain imperative; the legal force comes from the regulatory signs section, whose opening sentence is not among the passages. The image attached to m30 shows diamond (HOV) lane signs, not this sign, so the sign is named from the caption and no figure is linked.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle that bears [?this sign]

statements.text: FACT a "long" placard on the rear of a vehicle indicates a long commercial vehicle

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)

statements.note: The attached image (m67) shows a yellow placard with a truck silhouette and the word "LONG"; "rear signage" places it on the rear.

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. flags.note: Overlaps m85's ban on speeding up when another driver is trying to pass.

statements.note: The sanction itself is not among the passages, so no penalty is attached.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST move to the right AND MUST allow the passing vehicle to pass WHEN another driver is about to pass the driver

sources.quote: Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.
5. When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:

flags.note: Only the sample test question supplies "must"; the handbook text (m84) words the same duty as advice.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly as without a trailer

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

statements.note: "Cannot" here describes the vehicle's ability, not a prohibition.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer needs more space BECAUSE the vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. statements.force_from: imperative ("signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass")
statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal AND SHOULD pull over AND SHOULD let the other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass. Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them. If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

statements.note: The towing role comes from the Towing chapter and the heading "Being passed".

statements.text: a driver MUST stop WHEN the driver is approaching a stopped school bus that has its upper alternating red lights flashing, whether the driver is behind the bus or approaching the bus from the front, IF VIOLATED a [?heavy] fine AND 6 demerit points for a first offence

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

flags.note: No amount is given for the fine.

statements.note: The penalty comes from c5. This duty to stop is what makes passing such a school bus illegal (m77a).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m from the school bus WHEN the driver is coming from behind a stopped school bus that has its upper alternating red lights flashing

sources.quote: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.
You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

flags.note: Follows "You must stop" (c1); the handbook does not say whether the 20 m distance is law too.

statements.note: The stopped bus with its lights flashing comes from the neighbouring passage c1.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT go WHEN the driver has stopped for a school bus that has its upper alternating red lights flashing UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

sources.quote: Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.
You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

flags.note: Follows "You must stop" (c1); the handbook does not say whether staying stopped is law too.

statements.note: The stop for the school bus comes from the neighbouring passage c1.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO c1a WHEN the road has a median strip AND the driver is approaching the school bus from the front

sources.quote: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

statements.note: "Only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop" is read as switching c1a off for vehicles approaching from the front; vehicles from behind keep the duty.
